issues.description: The zero-valued data-directory constructor duplicates a spec-compatible struct literal instead of exposing the executable helper through dual_spec.
issues.rationale: The executable body is already the exact spec expression. In this snapshot the contract repeats the literal, leaving no spec-side Self::none() definition for other models to reuse. The pair-exec-helpers-with-spec-models guideline prefers dual_spec when one definition serves both modes. Review comment 4561893594 requests this change, and subsequent commit 12a489a1c6fa8d055f74a28b17302d0627d46468 adds #[verus_verify(dual_spec)] and changes the contract to returns Self::none().

issues.description: The crate-visible PE-header API exposes closed precondition and result models without caller-visible characterization, preventing callers outside the defining module from establishing the input obligation or interpreting the returned bytes.
issues.rationale: make_pe_coff_header is pub(crate), requires valid_setup_elf, and ensures a result characterized by pe_coff_bytes_spec (lines 283-288). Both models are pub(crate) closed at this snapshot, with no exported characterization lemma, so callers in other modules cannot derive the input obligation from its documented ELF conditions or unfold the result model. This is a modular contract-usability defect rather than only a preference for open declarations; private representation models need not all be opened. The fixed follow-up commit 12a489a1c6fa8d055f74a28b17302d0627d46468 makes the caller-facing models open while retaining packed representations behind a closed helper. The category is semantic, consistently with the API-contract findings in PR #797. This does not claim an executable runtime defect.
